Are you an ambitious researcher with a background in neuroscience or biomolecular science? As a PhD _tudent in our team, you will investigate how cell-type vulnerability or resilience impact neurodegeneration in the human brain using innovative proteomics other -omics techniques. Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) encompasses a group of neurodegenerative diseases that progressively affect behavior, movement, personality and/or language. We aim to identify the molecular and cellular causes of FTD that trigger its onset and early progression with the aim to design evidence-based treatment. We are looking for a highly motivated researcher to join our team. You will design and execute proteomics studies on human brain tissue of sporadic patients and human iPSC-derived neurons. The aim is to understand the molecular and cellular dysfunctions that lead to cell-type-specific vulnerability that may be causative to FTD through highly innovative single-cell and spatial (prote)-omics technologies. Would you like to know more about the different phases within the PhD trajectory? You can read more about this on this page. As a member of our team, you will: design and execute proteomics studies to identify cell-type specific vulnerability; perform experiments in human postmortem FTD brain tissue and patient iPSC-derived neuronal cell cultures; aid in data analysis and integration of -omics datasets to characterize cell-specific functional dysregulation and cellular crosstalk; contribute to scientific reporting, publications, and regulatory-ready data packages; supervise undergraduate _tudents; report on your findings in regular work meetings, conferences, and scientific publications in reputable journals. This position offers a unique opportunity to contribute to translational neuroscience in a dynamic team of proteomic and neuroscience researchers in the search for fun_amental insights with real-world therapeutic impact. You have: a master's degree in neuroscience, biomolecularscience, or biochemistry; proven expertise and skills with molecular and cellular work as part of an internship; experience with programming and data analysis (Python, R). Expertise with omics datasets is a strong advantage; strong written and verbal communication skills in English. We are looking for the following personality traits: excellent organisational and management skills; working diligently and with high accuracy; a team player who enjoys collaborating in an interdisciplinary environment; a creative and independent thinker who takes initiative. You will be employed by Amsterdam UMC Research BV. A contract for 12 months, with the intention to extend for a total of four years. The Guideline PhD contract applies to this vacancy. Classification in salary scale OIO: € 3.217 to € 4.077 gross for full-time employment (depending on experience). In addition to a good basic salary, we offer 8.3% end-of-year bonus. Calculate your net salary here. Holiday hours: 194.4 per year for full time and a possibility to save additional hours. 100% reimbursement for public transport travel costs. If you travel by foot, bicycle, or car, a mileage allowance of €0.21 per km applies (up to a maximum of 40 km one way by car). Do you prefer walking or cycling? Take advantage of our good bike scheme. Pension accrual with BeFrank, a modern, comprehensible and fairly priced pension. Watch this video with more information about joining Amsterdam UMC Research BV. The project is part of the larger Adore initiative, which aims to bring together cancer and neuroscience expertise and drive biomedical breakthroughs in both fields. This project is a clear example of that ambition, and you will work closely with researchers from both the Cancer Center Amsterdam, Center for Neurogenomics & Cognitive Research at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the Alzheimer Center Amsterdam UMC.
